parole.significato: favourite, darling (person who enjoys special regard or favor; person who is preferred or trusted above all others)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Favorit, from Middle French favorit (“favored one”), from favorir (“to favor”), from Latin favor (“good will, favor”).
Borrowed from German Möbel. Doublet of mobilny.

parole.significato: officer (person occupying a position from second lieutenant to marshal or an analogous positions in the uniformed servi…
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Offizier. First attested in 1656–1688. Compare Kashubian oficéra, Silesian ôficyr, and Slovincian ofcéra.

parole.significato: dress shoe (shoe worn on formal events)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Pantoffel, from Middle High German pantoffel, from Middle French, from Italian pantofola.

parole.significato: pale, picket (wooden stake driven into the ground forming part of a fence)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Stakete, Staket, from Middle French estakette, estachette, from Old French estache (“pole, stake”), a Germanic borrowing equalling German Staken, English stake from Proto-Germanic *stakô (“pole, stick, stake”) from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teg- (“pole, stick, stake”).
Borrowed from German Visier, from Middle French, from Old French visiere.
